title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 65-66
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 65 to 66 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'श्रीदः श्रीशः श्रीनिवासः श्रीनिधिः श्रीविभावनः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 65 to 66 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 65 to 66.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 65 to 66** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **श्रीदः श्रीशः श्रीनिवासः श्रीनिधिः श्रीविभावनः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:

**श्रीदः श्रीशः श्रीनिवासः श्रीनिधिः श्रीविभावनः । श्रीधरः श्रीकरः श्रेयः श्रीमाँल्लोकत्रयाश्रयः ॥** **स्वक्षः स्वङ्गः शतानन्दो नन्दिर्ज्योतिर्गणेश्वरः । विजितात्मा विधेयात्मा सत्कीर्तिश्छिन्नसंशयः ॥**

He gives prosperity, he is the lord of Shri and her abode. The treasure of Shri, the one who makes her grow, is that God of gods. He bears Shri and bestows her, he is the highest good and the refuge of the three worlds. Fair-eyed, fair of limb, with a hundred joys is he. Bliss, light and lord of the hosts is that God of gods. He has conquered himself, is self-disciplined, of good fame, and cuts every doubt.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 65 to 66 mean?
faq.a: He gives prosperity, he is the lord of Shri and her abode. The treasure of Shri, the one who makes her grow, is that God of gods. He bears Shri and bestows her, he is the highest good and the refuge of the three worlds. Fair-eyed, fair of limb, with a hundred joys is he. Bliss, light and lord of the hosts is that God of gods. He has conquered himself, is self-disciplined, of good fame, and cuts every doubt.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
